subject: Production tail regression impacting ApexSystems — request for exec-visible update
messages:
From: Liam O'Neil <liam@apexsystems.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-13T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 throughput spikes + 503s since model roll — logs attached

Jordan / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency (p95 -> ~2.1s, p99 -> ~6.8s) and intermittent 503s in our Hosted API calls beginning ~2028-06-13 15:40 UTC, immediately after you pushed the model variant labeled rm-v2-quant-optimized. Our backlog shows repeated OOM signals and GPU memory-related resets on a subset of hosts. I attached a sampling of request traces and a short timeline.

Customer impact: degraded user experience on our customer-facing chat product; estimated ~14% error rate for requests hitting the affected endpoints over the last 30m. This is blocking a payments rollout for a major partner.

What we need: an urgent RCA, immediate mitigation plan (rollback or mitigation config), and whether you can open an exec bridge — this is escalated internally.

Attachments: apex_request_trace_0613.log

Thanks,
Liam
Ops Lead, Apex Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam@apexsystems.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-13T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 throughput spikes + 503s since model roll — logs attached

Liam — thanks for the quick heads-up and the log bundle. We're standing up a short bridge for 17:30 PT to triage; invite sent.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Triage traces and correlate with host-level OOM signals (Dev)
- Snapshot KV/cache metrics and slab utilization for the model variant (Evelyn)
- Prepare a rollback plan for rm-v2-quant-optimized if we confirm regression

I appreciate the severity — we will prioritize. We'll aim to have a mitigation decision within 2 hours of the bridge.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-13T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial findings from customer traces (apex) — heads-up

Team — copying raw customer notes into thread. Key observations from a quick pass on the traces + our telemetry: 
- Rapid uptick in KV cache eviction rate coincident with request surge for rm-v2-quant-optimized.
- Elevated GPU memory fragmentation on ~12% of hosts serving Apex (kernel alloc failure traces seen).
- Several requests show repeated retry/queueing behavior hitting the serving runtime's batcher timeouts, then returning 503.

Hypothesis: a change in allocation pattern from the quantized kernels is causing slab fragmentation + increased KV eviction (more memory churn), which elevates worst-case latency (p99). Could also be aggravated by new default batch size heuristics in the runtime.

Attachments: runtime-metrics-snapshot-0613.csv

Can you prioritize a host-level heap/allocator dump from one of the affected nodes and surface any recent allocator/quantization kernel changes?

-J
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: initial findings from customer traces (apex) — diagnosis + short mitigations

Quick update after retrieving allocator counters and host profiles from two affected machines: 
- Confirmed high slab fragmentation leading to transient OOM path on the inference engine's memory manager for quantized kernels.
- KV cache TTL was low for this customer (configured to aggressive eviction), amplifying memory churn.
- Kernel selection change in last runtime rollout (opt-quant-kernel-picker v1.3) is selecting a new allocator path that increases small-allocation churn.

Immediate mitigations applied (2028-06-14 08:45 PT):
1) Pinned Apex requests to the previous model variant rm-v1-stable for affected customer routes (hotfix routing) — this reduced 503s and moved p95 back toward baseline.
2) Raised per-shard KV cache TTL + temporarily disabled prefix prefetch to reduce eviction thrash.
3) Short-term allocator change: lowered small allocation bins threshold to reduce fragmentation (mitigation_patch.diff attached).

Results so far: p95 improved significantly; p99 still elevated due to a subset of slow hosts (we're isolating them). Will continue with Canary rollback of opt-quant-kernel-picker v1.3 tomorrow morning if p99 remains high.

- Dev
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam@apexsystems.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Customer update: mitigations applied and next steps (ApexSystems)

Liam — thanks for the patience on the bridge earlier. Short update: 
- We applied targeted routing to rm-v1-stable for your affected routes and increased KV TTLs; that removed the surge of 503s and brought p95 back within your SLOs.
- We observed persistent p99 tails on a small subset (~3–5%) of calls coming from a handful of hosts. Dev's team applied a reduced small-allocation threshold patch which helped on some hosts but a full kernel-picker rollback is scheduled for a canary tomorrow at 04:00 PT.

Requests for you:
- Please share any additional host-side core dumps if you have them (we requested access during the bridge).
- If you can tolerate the canary rollback window, we'll run it and monitor; if stable we'll do a wider rollback within 3 hours.

We've opened ticket HS-34219 and uploaded bridge notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/cs/apexsystems/bridge-notes-0613

I'll follow up with an exec-visible summary after the canary.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary: ApexSystems outage window & recommended customer remediation/compensation

Team — preparing a short exec-friendly summary to share with leadership and finance. Key points: 
- Issue: New runtime kernel selection (opt-quant-kernel-picker v1.3) increased small-allocation churn on quantized model execution paths, which increased slab fragmentation and triggered transient OOM behavior on a subset of GPU hosts. This amplified request-level retry behavior and produced p99 tail regressions for ApexSystems.
- Impact: ~14% error rate at peak (503s), p95 normalized after routing to rm-v1-stable and KV/allocator mitigations; p99 remains elevated until canary rollback completes. Customer reported business impact on partner rollout.
- Actions taken: hotpatch routing to rm-v1-stable, raised KV TTLs, applied allocator threshold patch (mitigation_patch.diff), scheduled canary rollback of opt-quant-kernel-picker v1.3 (04:00 PT).
- Request: approval to offer a one-time credit of 25% of the previous month's Hosted API spend for ApexSystems (deal APX-778) conditioned on closure of RCA and postmortem within 5 business days. Also recommend priority postmortem and changes to our rollout checklist (add fragmentation smoke tests and opt-quant rollback guard).

I'll brief Execs if Marcus wants to join; please advise on the credit approval and any additional communication to the customer.

--
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
